ledger.claim: The rider's own trip record and the platform's GPS trace agree that this trip was driven 24.6 km against a booked optimal route of 20.0 km — an excess of 4.6 km, or 23.0% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass: the excess exceeds 20% of optimal and exceeds 0.8 km absolute. The deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own evidence.

The governing distance figure is the trace, not the rounded trip-record copy: POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the field that governs the threshold test, and here the trace records 24.6 km with 100.0% coverage, 193 fixes at a 10 s interval and no gaps. The measurement is clean and unimpaired.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and discharges it: the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02839 and the same pickup/start timestamp of 2026-08-21T18:23:08+08:00, and the excess of 4.6 km / 23.0% meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden now shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause.

The driver's asserted excuse — 'KPE closed, LTA advisory on file' — is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. The advisory on file (ADV-20260821-009) is a KPE closure with a validity window of 17:53–19:20 on 2026-08-21, which does overlap the trip window, so the driver's assertion is not weightless on its face; the question is whether the trace actually left the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoined after, which is the POL-RD-03(c) limb.

The trace never enters the advisory's own geometry: the derived advisory-area test records 0 fixes inside the advisory area and a minimum distance of 1350.67 m from it. The driver's route did not pass through the closed KPE segment the advisory describes, so the closure cannot explain the 4.6 km of excess measured on this trip.

Even if the closure were accepted as an external cause, POL-RD-03 caps exoneration at min(measured_excess, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km - optimal_distance_km) + 1.00). Here that is min(4.6, 1.30 x (23.0 - 20.0) + 1.00) = min(4.6, 4.90) = 4.6 km, so the cap does not bite and the full measured excess stands as the figure to be refunded.

The rider was charged SGD 3.00 for the ECP Fort Rd eastbound gantry, and the fare_breakdown records that gantry as NOT on the optimal route. The trace's nearest fix to that gantry is 59.12 m, within the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09 uses, so the gantry was crossed — but it was crossed on a corridor the optimal route does not use. That is an off-route pass-through the rider did not cause.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, not discretionary. The fare model is METERED, so recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 20.0 + 0.28 x 27.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 on-optimal-route ERP = 27.16. Charged_total is 35.01. Refund = 35.01 - 27.16 = 7.85, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

The off-route ERP of SGD 3.00 is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund, because the recomputed fare includes only on-optimal-route gantries and the ECP Fort Rd gantry is recorded as off-route. Under POL-RD-09(1) it is itemised for transparency but must NOT be added on top of the 7.85 figure — the rider's total recovery is the POL-RD-02 refund alone.

The driver's profile shows a trailing-90-day deviation flag count of 1 against 197 completed trips — a ratio of 0.005, far below the 0.05 threshold, and the absolute count is below 3. No repeat-deviation pattern is established under POL-RD-06, so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral is available on this record. I concede this point.

The rider's profile shows 0 deviation claims in the trailing 60 days and 0 substantiated, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration uplift for a serial claimant does not apply and the rider's claim stands on the trace alone without any additional corroboration requirement.

The chat log for this trip is empty — 0 messages — so no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 can be made out, and no waypoint_hint exists to corroborate one. The driver cannot invoke POL-RD-04 on this record.

The trip_record shows no pickup or dropoff amendment — pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null — so POL-RD-05 relocation does not apply and the booked optimal of 20.0 km is the correct baseline.
The vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply and the solo optimal of 20.0 km governs.

The rider's own claim is that the trip ran 24.6 km against a booked optimal of 20.0 km. The governing measurement is the trace, not the rounded trip-record copy: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 24.6 km against trip_record.optimal_distance_km of 20.0 km, an excess of 4.6 km and 23.00% — both above the POL-RD-01 establishment tests (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%). The deviation is established on this trip's own trace.

The excess of 4.6 km is below the 8.0 km absolute materiality gate and below 50% of the 20.0 km optimal, so this is an established but NOT material deviation. POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is therefore not triggered by materiality, and the driver's deviation_flags_90d of 1 against 197 completed trips in 90 days (0.0051) would not meet the 3-flag or 0.05-ratio pattern test in any event. No repeat-deviation uplift or conduct referral is available on this record.

The driver's only stated excuse is 'KPE closed, LTA advisory on file'. The bundle does contain a live LTA advisory for the KPE towards ECP after Defu Flyover, active 17:53–19:20 on the trip date, overlapping the trip window, with a shortest lawful alternative of 23.0 km. That is a real advisory naming a real segment, so the driver's assertion is not weightless under POL-RD-08 — but the advisory's own geometry is a small box (lat 1.3549–1.371, lng 103.8587–103.8658) and the trace records zero fixes inside it, with a minimum approach of 1350.67 m. The trace never enters the advisory area, so the limb (c) requirement that the actual route leave the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoin after is not made out on the record.

Even if the closure were accepted as the cause, POL-RD-03 caps exoneration at min(measured_excess, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km - optimal_distance_km) + 1.00) = min(4.6, 1.30 x (23.0 - 20.0) + 1.00) = min(4.6, 4.90) = 4.6 km. The cap does not bite here, so the closure-adjusted optimal would be 24.6 km and the excess would fall to zero. The rider's case therefore turns entirely on whether the trace actually took the closure diversion — and the trace's own advisory-area test says it did not.

The rider's second complaint — 'an ERP gantry I would never have passed' — is borne out by the fare ledger. The single ERP line is ECP Fort Rd eastbound, SGD 3.00, charged at 18:37:08, and the fare breakdown itself records on_optimal_route = false for that gantry. The trace's nearest fix to the gantry is 59.12 m at 18:39:08, which is within the 250 m crossing radius, so the gantry was physically crossed — but it was crossed on a corridor the optimal route does not use. That is an off-route pass-through charge, and under POL-RD-09(2) it is refunded to the rider as a standalone correction even where the distance and time charges stand.

The distance and time refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02. The fare model is METERED, so recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 20.0 + 0.28 x 27.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 on-optimal-route ERP = (3.80 + 15.00 + 7.56) + 0.80 = 27.16. Charged_total is 35.01, so the refund is 35.01 - 27.16 = 7.85, which is 22.42% of charged_total — well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and well below the 90% full-refund share. The payable figure rounds up to SGD 7.85.

The rider's contested amount is SGD 7.00 and the POL-RD-02 arithmetic yields SGD 7.85, so the rider is made whole on the contested sum and slightly more. The rider's claim is supported by admissible, complete evidence: the trip record, the trace and the fare ledger all carry trip_id TRP-02839 and the same pickup timestamp, satisfying POL-RD-08(a), and the excess satisfies POL-RD-08(b) on an unimpaired trace. The rider has discharged the initial burden and the driver has pointed to no clause that survives the trace.

The trace is clean for policy purposes: 193 fixes at a 10 s sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, and no straight-line jump over 500 m. POL-RD-07(a) to (c) are not met, so no corroboration requirement attaches and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation is triggered. The admissibility pre-pass agrees, tagging the artifact COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

The chat log is empty — zero messages, no first or last message timestamp. There is therefore no rider instruction in the record that could exonerate any part of the excess under POL-RD-04, and no waypoint_hint to test. The driver has not claimed a rider-requested detour, and none is available on this record.

The trip record shows no amendment to either endpoint: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-05 cannot be run and no amended optimal exists to displace the booked 20.0 km baseline. The vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply either.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: this is the ruling on trip TRP-02839.

DISTANCE. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02839) records 24.6 km against the booked optimal route of 20.0 km (EV-TRIP-02839) — an excess of 4.6 km, or 23.00% of optimal. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure the governing one, and both of its tests are met (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so the deviation is established. It is not a material deviation (below 8.0 km and below 50%), so POL-RD-06's repeat-deviation check is not triggered; in any event the driver's trailing-90-day record (1 flag against 197 completed trips, 0.5%) is far below the 3-flag / 5% pattern, so there is no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral on this record.

THE CLOSURE. The driver's explanation — 'KPE closed, LTA advisory on file' — is tested against the traffic advisory for this trip and nothing else. An advisory is indeed on file: EV-ADVIS-02839-01, KPE towards ECP after Defu Flyover, active 17:53–19:20 with a shortest lawful alternative of 23.0 km, so it overlaps the trip window. But POL-RD-03 also requires the actual route to leave the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoin it afterwards, and that is not made out: the trace records zero fixes inside the advisory's area and never comes closer than 1,350.67 m to it. The optimal route's own polyline is not in the record, so this proximity test is the closest the record allows and it does not by itself decide the limb — but nothing else supplies it either. The closure therefore does not explain the excess, the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13, and no amended optimal is produced. The closure cap (1.30 x (23.0 - 20.0) + 1.00 = 4.90 km) is consequently never reached, because the exoneration it caps was not established.

REFUND. The fare model is METERED and the surge multiplier is 1.0, read from the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02839). Under POL-RD-02:
- charged_total = SGD 35.01
- recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 20.0 + 0.28 x 27.0) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 on-optimal-route ERP = SGD 27.16
- refund = 35.01 - 27.16 = SGD 7.85, which rounds up to SGD 7.85.
That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and below 90% of the charge, so it is a partial refund rather than a full one.

THE ERP LINE. The SGD 3.00 ECP Fort Rd eastbound charge (EV-FARE-02839) is recorded as lying off the optimal route, but the trace passes within 59.12 m of that gantry, so the gantry was in fact crossed and this is not a phantom line under POL-RD-09(4) — no billing-integrity referral arises. Because the deviation is refunded under POL-RD-02, that off-route ERP is already comprehended in the SGD 7.85 under POL-RD-09(1) and is itemised for transparency only; it must not be added on top. POL-RD-09(2)'s standalone pass-through correction applies only where a deviation is exonerated under POL-RD-03, which did not happen here. Total recovery is therefore SGD 7.85, not SGD 7.85 + SGD 3.00.

You contested SGD 7.00. The POL-RD-02 computation is arithmetic, not discretionary, and it yields SGD 7.85, so that is the sum refunded — slightly more than the amount in dispute.

NO ESCALATION. Trip identifiers and timestamps match across the trip record, trace and fare ledger; the trace is complete and unimpaired (193 fixes at 10-second intervals, no gaps); the refund is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling and below the charged total; and no charge line lacks a counterpart. The chat log is empty (no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 and no uncorroborated instruction under POL-RD-14), there is no endpoint amendment (POL-RD-05) and the vehicle is not a pooled one (POL-RD-12), so none of those clauses shifts the 20.0 km baseline. The profile artifacts are context only under POL-GEN-01 and established nothing about this trip.

The refund of SGD 7.85 is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so it issues for execution; either party may appeal within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
